flashcards.back: A feeding level in a food chain or web: producers are the first level, herbivores the second, and carnivores the levels above.
A sequence of trophic levels showing who eats whom, with arrows pointing in the direction of energy flow, from food to feeder.
All the interlinked food chains in a community, showing every feeding pathway energy can take.
A diagram of the energy at each trophic level, narrowing upwards because only about 10% of energy moves up each level.
An organism, usually a green plant, that captures sunlight by photosynthesis and feeds the whole food chain or web.
An organism that obtains energy by eating other organisms: primary consumers eat producers, secondary consumers eat herbivores.
An organism that breaks down dead matter and waste, releasing carbon and other matter back into cycles.
The cycling of carbon between air, living organisms and decomposers: photosynthesis draws CO2 in, respiration and combustion return it.

The "cycle of life" language makes energy sound like it loops round forever. Energy flows one way - sunlight in, heat out: what is recycled is matter - carbon, nitrogen and water. In the animation scene s6 the red energy dot enters as sunlight and leaves as heat, never returning, while the blue carbon dot loops round and round: matter cycles, energy does not.

items.answer: Most energy is lost as heat from respiration, in egestion and excretion, and in uneaten or undigested parts, so only about a tenth is built into new tissue that the next level can eat.
items.prompt: Explain why only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next level, and what happens to the rest.

items.answer: Habitat loss and fragmentation left fragments too small and isolated to support the species
items.prompt: A forest is cleared into small isolated fragments and a wide-ranging species disappears. What is the best explanation?

items.answer: Energy flows one way: sunlight in, heat out. Carbon cycles: photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants, while respiration, combustion and decomposition return CO2 to the air.
items.prompt: Compare how energy and carbon move through an ecosystem: state which one cycles and which flows one way, naming the processes involved.
